decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elbow-up approach toward the blue piece, gradually pitching the wrist downward; left stays home.
Move above the blue piece with a downward gripper, aligning the jaws to its narrow sides; inspect before closing.
Center the blue piece between the fingers using the wrist view, lower to its sides, and close.
Lift the closed blue grasp and carry it above the rightmost, shortest peg; verify retention and alignment.
Lower the blue piece toward its short peg while bringing the left arm into a gradual elbow-up, downward approach.
Seat and release the blue piece, then withdraw vertically. Position the left gripper above the nearby star for visual centering.
Center and close around the left star. Retract from the released blue and approach the right yellow square without crossing arms.
Lift the left star and carry it toward the tallest left peg. Approach the right square from above, using a conservative pregrasp height.
Fine-align and lower the held star over the left peg. Center the right square, descend to its edges, and close.
Correct the star toward the visible peg with clearance; lift and carry the square to the third peg while maintaining closed grasps.
Separate the wrists by moving the held square rightward and higher, while lowering the star along the visible left peg.
Make a small star-to-peg correction, lower gently, release and lift to inspect seating; keep the right square safely held aside.
The released star appears offset behind the peg. Regrasp and lift it for a corrected insertion rather than assuming seating.
Align the star with the actual peg tip visible below it, moving slightly right and toward the robot before a cautious descent.
The peg is now visible inside the star hole. Lower along it, open the gripper at the base, and withdraw to verify seating.
The first star is visibly on its peg. Approach the next left star while bringing the held square over the third peg, keeping the wrists separated.
Clear the right wrist sideways with the square held. Refine the left approach to the next star using the wrist image before closing.
Descend the centered left gripper to the second star and close; retain the right square clear of the left workspace.
Recenter the low star in the jaws at grasp height, then close around its sides rather than its upper tips.
Lift the second star and move it left to clear the central workspace. Bring the retained square above the third peg for visual alignment.
The left star was not retained; approach another left star open. Lower the square toward its peg while checking the hole rather than the rear peg segment.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for motion. Seat and release the square; center the left star at finger height and close.
Square seating is uncertain after release; withdraw the right arm and let it settle. Shift the left fingers toward the star body before reclosing.
Lift the newly centered star and carry it above the first peg, accounting for its slight lateral offset in the jaws. Keep the right arm clear.
Use the visible seated star and peg as the reference, correcting the held star rightward and slightly forward while approaching insertion height.
Align the held star with the first peg's exposed lower tip, correcting left before a small insertion descent.
The peg overlaps the star hole but the piece is tilted. Make a small centering correction, release near the stack, and lift to inspect gravity seating.
Clear the left wrist from the tilted star and inspect the blue piece closely with the right gripper open before correcting its seating.
Approach the blue piece itself, which is forward of the right jaws, for reseating. Bring the left gripper above the remaining table square.
Grasp the centered left square across its body and test a small lift. Close the right jaws around the blue piece at a conservative reseating height.
Reopen and lower around the blue body's sides for a small lift test. Move the held square toward a clear front staging area without crossing the arms.
Reposition the right grasp toward the blue body's center, then test retention by lifting. Lower and release the left square in a clear front staging spot.
Carry the regrasped blue slightly toward the robot and right, over the short peg, then descend cautiously. Withdraw the left arm from its released staging square.
Lower the blue along its now-centered peg, release, and withdraw. Approach the left orange disk with the other arm.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged observation. Center the left disk and approach the tilted right square with open grippers.
Center and lift the orange disk with the left arm. Regrasp the tilted square across its middle with the right arm, remaining on its own side.
Carry the retained orange disk inward but stop short of the right wrist. Reopen and lower to the square's actual sides, then close and test a lift.
Lift the retained square clear, then bring it back over the third peg using the seated blue as a position reference. Keep the orange disk held clear on the left.
Lower the square toward the third peg without lateral motion, retaining it until the peg-to-hole relationship is visible at insertion height.
Finish the square insertion with a small centering correction, release at the base, and withdraw vertically to inspect whether it stays flat.
The square did not seat; clear the right wrist before revisiting it. Bring the retained orange disk over the second peg for direct hole-to-tip alignment.
Refine the orange disk over the second peg using head-view geometry, then descend slightly. Approach the next orange disk from the right workspace.
Lower and release the orange disk at its peg, then inspect its settling. Center the next disk across its body before closing the right gripper.
Withdraw the open left fingers completely so the released disk can settle. Lift the right disk and keep it safely separated while inspecting the board.
The disks were not seated or retained. Clear the right arm and approach the orange disk beside the second peg for regrasping; require a visible peg inside the hole before release.
Regrasp the orange disk at its actual table height, with the hole centered between the jaws, then make a small retention-test lift.
The disk remained below the closed fingers. Reopen, shift toward its body at table height, close, and test retention with a short lift.
Correct the rejected tensor with no motion compensation. Lift the disk clear, then shift toward the robot to align over the second peg.
Lower the held disk over the second peg without releasing yet. Approach the next disk farther forward with the right gripper open and the arms separated.
The left disk has the peg visibly inside its hole; seat it and release. Center the right disk at finger height, close, and test a short lift.
The first orange disk is seated. Clear the left arm; reopen and lower the right jaws to the remaining disk's true side height, then retest retention.
Refine the right disk grasp slightly deeper and farther into its body, then test lift. Approach the remaining flat left star open for visual centering.
Recenter the disk within the jaw contact region and test a larger lift. Center and close on the flat left star at table-side height, keeping the arms separated.
Both lift tests were empty. Reopen and approach the actual object bodies at table height, correcting for the wrist image shift during descent; inspect before closing.
The objects are now at finger height. Make small body-centering corrections, close both grippers, and lift vertically to verify retention.
Carry the retained star above the first peg. Move the retained disk to a clear front-center staging area for left-arm access without crossing arms.
Lower the star to peg-entry height while retaining it. Set the orange disk on the front staging area, open, and lift the right gripper clear.
Make a small star-to-peg correction and continue a shallow descent without releasing. Clear the right wrist from the staged disk.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged observation. Lift and recenter the held star; approach the remaining right star without crossing arms.
Lift and offset the held star to expose the peg tip before realignment. Bring the right star into the jaw contact region at table height, still open.
